title: Zodiacal light at La SIlla
caption: Zodiacal light over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Rising from the horizon at La Silla, a roughly triangular, diffuse white glow reaches up into the night sky. This is zodiacal light, which seems to extend from the neighbourhood of the Sun along the ecliptic, the band of the zodiac.

The glow comes from sunlight scattered by dust spread between the planets in the plane of the Solar System. The Sun itself is below the horizon, but its light still reaches those dust grains and is scattered toward us.

In spring and autumn, when the zodiac rises steeply from the horizon, the best times to look are just after sunset or just before sunrise. That tilt helps lift the glow higher, out of the thick air near the ground, so it is easier to see from a dark site like this one.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based photograph by Zdeněk Bardon. The source does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Zodiacal light is diffuse and faint, and a camera gathering light over time may show it more plainly than the eye.
